tasks.title: Create packages/shared/version.mjs
tasks.intent: Create packages/shared/version.mjs containing the single definition `export const VERSION = "1";` so every consumer derives the value from one place.

tasks.title: Point packages/a at the shared constant
tasks.intent: Replace the local `export const VERSION = "1";` in packages/a/index.mjs with `import { VERSION } from "../shared/version.mjs"; export { VERSION };` (import-plus-re-export so the local template literal in aInfo keeps a binding), leaving aInfo() behavior unchanged. Do not touch the test file.

tasks.title: Point packages/b at the shared constant
tasks.intent: Same change in packages/b/index.mjs: import VERSION from ../shared/version.mjs, re-export it, keep bInfo() unchanged. T002 and T003 write disjoint files and can run in either order after T001.

tasks.title: Run suite and file acceptance
tasks.intent: Confirm MONO-001-A (packages/shared/version.mjs exists) and execute MONO-002-A: node --test "tests/*.test.mjs" with exit 0. The pre-existing tests/version.test.mjs pins VERSION equality across packages and both info() outputs, so a green run proves the re-exports preserve behavior.

observations.statement: packages/a/index.mjs and packages/b/index.mjs each define VERSION = "1" locally; tests/version.test.mjs imports VERSION from both packages and asserts equality plus aInfo()/bInfo() outputs, making it the existing-behavior coverage for the transition.

A re-export written as `export { VERSION } from ...` does not create a local binding, so the package files must use import-plus-re-export to keep their template literals working; the plan spells this out to prevent a runtime ReferenceError.
